newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: "Death plot" deception by Salinas - Mexican editor.
newsitem.headline: "Death plot" deception by Salinas - Mexican editor.

text.p: A prizewinning Mexican newspaper editor accused former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari on Tuesday of playing up conspiracy theories of a 1994 assassination to divert attention from Mexico's other woes.

J. Jesus Blancornelas, at the United Nations for a news conference before receiving a journalism award, said his investigations showed that the March 23, 1994, killing of ruling party presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio was carried out by one man acting alone.
Colosio, shot in the head and abdomen, almost certainly would have become president. The killing was the most serious political assassination in Mexico in half a century.

Colosio was Salinas's choice as candidate of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which has ruled Mexico for 67 consecutive years. His replacement, Ernest Zedillo, easily won the 1994 election.

Blancornelas, editor in chief of the Zeta weekly in Tijuana, was one of four winners of the Freedom Prize of the New York-based Committee to Protect Journalists for his exposure of corruption and drug trafficking in Mexico.

He said Salinas was facing the Zapatista insurrection in the south of Mexico and a seriously troubled economy. "So he thought that it was convenient that the murder was seen outside of Mexico as a kind of plot against Mexico," he said.

No comment was available from Salinas, who is living in self-imposed exile in Ireland. He left Mexico in disgrace in March 1995 after the arrest of his elder brother Raul on charges that Raul masterminded a separate political killing in Mexico in September 1994.
Newspapers in Mexico reported on Tuesday that prosecutors were flying to Ireland to interview the former president about the Colosio murder. Officials would neither confirm nor deny the reports.
Blancornelas said he had given his information to investigators and was being called to testify.
Mario Aburto Martinez is serving a 45-year prison sentence for shooting Colosio in the head.

Colosio was also shot in the abdomen, but an accused second gunman was freed by a judge in August for lack of evidence against him. Several accused co-conspirators have also been freed for lack of evidence.
Prosecutors and most Mexicans still believe the killing was a plot involving top PRI politicians, drug traffickers or both.
